resolution.justification: Rounding model kept at the native 0.1 cm so that the decimal digit can separate measured from written-in heights; diurnal height change is handled by measurement_variability, not by coarsening.

population.repeat_cases: later cases of the same patient usually copy the height; use the first-case posterior

special_values.off_grid: values finer than 0.1 cm (1 value, 157.36) are flagged off_grid and rounded to 0.1 before evaluation

flags.possibly_written_in: posterior weight of the tens, whole_cm, half_cm and round_up modes; > 0 only for values ending in .0 or .5

measured.basis: Adult stature falls about 14-17 mm over the day, mostly in the first hours after rising (Leatt, Reilly & Troup 1986; Healey et al. 2011; Voss & Bailey 1997). With time of measurement unknown, a uniform loss over ~1.5 cm has SD ~0.43 cm; combined with stadiometer reproducibility SD ~0.3 cm (Voss & Bailey 1997) gives ~0.5 cm.

written_in.basis: 2018 Korea Community Health Survey, 171,384 adults: self-reported minus measured height by sex and age; limits of agreement -6.26 to 4.31 cm give SD ~2.6 cm. Assumes written-in heights are self-reported. True height = recorded - bias.

references: Leatt P, Reilly T, Troup JG. Spinal loading during circuit weight-training and running. Br J Sports Med 1986;20(3):119-24.
Voss LD, Bailey BJR. Diurnal variation in stature: is stretching the answer? Arch Dis Child 1997;77:319-22.
Differences in accuracy of height, weight, and BMI between self-reported and measured using the 2018 Korea Community Health Survey data. Epidemiol Health 2022 (PMC9117107).
